subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw make retained session transcripts durable by default, and if so what archive naming/location and cleanup policy should replace the shipped `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` behavior?
rationale: The code change is not just a suffix swap: it changes shipped filename semantics, config behavior, cleanup guarantees, and operator expectations around transcript retention.

options.title: Adopt durable archives
options.body: Rename or relocate retained transcripts under a durable archive contract, disable hard removal by default, and add migration/doctor/docs/tests for existing archives.

options.title: Clarify but keep cleanup
options.body: Keep physical cleanup available but split naming and retention knobs so retained transcripts are not described as deleted until they are actually removed.

options.title: Keep current lifecycle
options.body: Leave `.deleted.*` and retention cleanup as-is and close this as an accepted operator-script/documentation risk.

recommendation.title: Adopt durable archives
recommendation.body: Rename or relocate retained transcripts under a durable archive contract, disable hard removal by default, and add migration/doctor/docs/tests for existing archives.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session maintenance seam work is the closest current-main ownership signal for coordinating the config, cleanup, and migration boundary.
